subject: Veridian DPA: private deployment boundaries and customer KMS
messages:
From: Sarah Bell <sarah.bell@veridian.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@veridian.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0500
Subject: Private deployment questions — KMS, subprocessors, and international transfers

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. We're preparing our internal legal and infosec packet for a private VPC deployment of Redwood for clinical NLP workloads. A few items where we need concrete language for our DPA and operational runbook: 

- Customer-controlled keys: we need confirmation that customer CMKs (AWS KMS) can be used for encrypting model inputs and outputs in transit and at rest, and that Redwood personnel will not have decrypt permissions.
- Operator access: what exact admin actions require operator access and what logs/justifications are captured when operator access is exercised?
- Subprocessors: please provide a current list (or an evergreen link) of subprocessors that will handle telemetry, backups, or infra support for private deployments.
- Cross-border transfers: our data residency team requires a short statement about whether any telemetry or support logs may transit outside the EU and what safeguards are in place.

I've attached our security questionnaire (first tab) and a redline doc with DPA items we've been asked to escalate. Can someone from your team respond with suggested DPA language and a short ops runbook excerpt? We have an internal deadline of Dec 10.

Appreciate the help —
Sarah

--
Sarah Bell
Head of Security & Privacy
Veridian Therapeutics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bell <sarah.bell@veridian.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 13:20:00 +0000
Subject: RE: Private deployment questions — proposed DPA language and operator controls

Sarah — appreciate the detailed questionnaire. Below are proposed short-form clauses you can drop into the DPA (we're open to negotiation on wording):

1) Customer-controlled keys (proposed clause):
"Customer shall provision and manage the cryptographic key(s) (\"Customer Key(s)\") used to encrypt Customer Data in the private deployment environment. Customer Key material shall be stored in Customer-managed KMS under Customer control. Redwood shall not be granted Decrypt or ExportKey permissions on Customer Keys as a condition of normal operation. In limited emergency scenarios where break-glass access is required for remediation, Redwood operator actions shall be time-limited, approved through an auditable approval flow, and recorded in the audit trail provided to Customer."

2) Operator access & logging (proposed clause):
"Operator access to customer infrastructure is limited to the actions described in the Deployment Runbook and requires (i) an approval ticket, and (ii) multifactor authentication tied to the operator identity. All operator sessions are logged (session start/end, commands executed, reason, approver) and logs are forwarded to Customer-designated log endpoints. Redwood will provide monthly summaries of operator access events and make full session logs available for on-site audit within agreed SLAs."

3) Subprocessors (summary):
We maintain a live subprocessors registry (link in attachments). For private deployments the common subprocessors are: NimbusOps (infrastructure support), LogHarbor (log collection), and CloudMirror (backup replication). We propose adding a DPA schedule that references the live registry and commits to 30-day notice before material subprocessor changes.

4) Cross-border telemetry:
"Operational telemetry necessary for support (e.g., control-plane metrics, anonymized health pings) may be transmitted to Redwood regions outside the EU for processing; Customer Data (model inputs/outputs) shall remain within the Customer VPC unless Customer explicitly authorizes transfer. Any telemetry leaving the EU will be minimized and subject to pseudonymization and standard contractual protections."

We can provide a short ops runbook snippet describing the exact approval workflow, and a network diagram showing which endpoints may be contacted. Laura — can you attach the diagram and a one-page runbook excerpt?

-karthik

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:45:00 +0000
Subject: RE: diagrams and ops runbook excerpt

Sarah — attaching the diagram and a short ops excerpt (see attachments). Key operational points: 
- Customer KMS: we support using a Customer CMK with an external key policy preventing Redwood's IAM role from calling Decrypt/GenerateDataKey without an explicit temporary grant.
- Break-glass: temporary grants are issued via an automated ticket system requiring at least two approvers (customer security rep + Redwood on-call), TTL limited to 30 minutes, and all actions recorded.
- Backup and replication: backup snapshots can be encrypted using customer keys; replication targets are configurable and default to customer-controlled storage in the same region.
- Support logs: agent heartbeats and aggregated health metrics are permitted to leave the VPC; full payloads are not captured.

If you want tighter guarantees (no telemetry leaving the VPC at all), we can offer a lockbox configuration on private deployments that disables outbound telemetry by default — this is a managed option with increased operational cost.

Laura

Laura Bennett

From: Sarah Bell <sarah.bell@veridian.com>

Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Private deployment questions — KMS, subprocessors, and international transfers

Thanks — this is very helpful. A few follow-ups from our legal team after reviewing your proposed phrasing: 
- They want explicit confirmation that model checkpoints/weights are never exfiltrated or made available to Redwood. Can you confirm that the control plane cannot package or export model artifacts from the customer's environment?
- For the subprocessor registry: can we get a signed attestation that the subprocessors adhere to the same contractual security standards (or an addendum)?

We can accept the break-glass flow but will ask to shorten the TTL to 15 minutes and require an out-of-band confirmation to the customer's security pager for emergency access.

I'll send the questionnaire back with inline comments. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Sarah
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Bell <sarah.bell@veridian.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Veridian DPA: follow-ups and attestations

Sarah — quick note from the compliance team: we can add a vendor attestation appendix for core subprocessors and will commit to a 30-day notice for subprocessor changes. Regarding model artifacts: by design the serving runtime does not export model weights or checkpoints from the customer-controlled environment; that capability is restricted to customer-side model management tools. We'll add explicit language to the DPA stating "Redwood shall not export, copy, or retain model checkpoints or weights from the Customer environment."

On TTL: we can accept 15 minutes for emergency grants and we support an out-of-band notification requirement (pager/email to named security contacts). Final wording will be in the DPA redline — happy to iterate.

Thanks,
Monica
